newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yen yield curve flattening on DKB scandal--traders.
newsitem.headline: Yen yield curve flattening on DKB scandal--traders.

text.p: Japan's debt yield curve is going through an unusual flattening, with short-term yields underpinned by strong fund demand from scandal-hit Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB).
Senior traders said on Thursday that DKB was willing to offer rates a few basis points higher than other banks, pushing up the market level.
DKB, at the centre of a racketeer payoff scandal, is anxious to secure funds in case further bad news for the beleaguered bank triggers heavy deposit withdrawals, they said.
Individual depositors pulled out nearly 150 billion yen worth of funds from the bank in May alone.
Meanwhile, long-term yields have fallen due to lessening signs of a rise in Japanese interest rates.

"Because DKB's offer rate is higher than that of others and is in a large volume, they cannot help but raise the offer rates. Thus, short-term interest rates remained high despite recent falls in the long-term bond yields," said Shin Nagai, vice president at ABN AMRO Bank in Tokyo.
If it were not for the scandal, three-month euroyen cash interest rates could have fallen to around 0.55 percent from the current level of around 0.62 percent, Nagai said.
After a recent series of weak economic data, Japan's long-term bond yields started to fall again. This was after briefly recovering from a dip to record low levels in early April.
Stronger Tokyo stocks since the beginning of May triggered speculation that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) may end its ultra-accommodative credit stance in the coming months.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) rose as high as 2.75 percent after hitting a record low of 2.075 percent on April 8.

But sentiment over the outlook for the economy worsened again on a growing view that the yen's recent rise against the dollar may slow exports. Also, Japan's economic recovery has been affected by the rise in the sales tax to five percent from three percent from April 1.
The key 182nd 10-year JGB yield fell to 2.360 percent in late afternoon trade on Thursday.
"The bond market will not be affected by the scandal unless DKB decides to cut back its JGB holdings," said Kenichi Hirao, manager of the fixed income division at Sakura Securities Co.
Since prosecutors raided DKB's headquarters on May 20, ten senior DKB officials have been arrested in connection with the payoff scandal, which also involves Nomura Securities Co Ltd .
A senior dealer at a city bank said banks and other fund-raisers have been at a disadvantage against fund suppliers since the payoff scandal ensnared DKB.
But he said complaints about DKB have been muted because it is a major player in the market.
"This case is different from in the past when smaller banks faced financial problems and they were forced to leave the market," he said.
The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Wednesday it was suspending DKB from JGB auctions and underwriting for the time being, the same measures it took against Nomura on May 13.
